title: Evaluation of Perimenopausal Symptoms and Their Impact on the Quality of Life Among Women in Albania
content: Introduction: Perimenopause represents a critical transitional phase in a woman's life, during which hormonal fluctuations can significantly impair her quality of life. This study evaluates the demographic profile, symptomatology, and information sources of women in Albania, analyzing the extent to which this transition impacts their professional, social, and family daily life. Methods: A descriptive quantitative study (2026) was conducted with a sample of 120 women aged 35–50 years in Albania, selected via random sampling. Data collection was carried out using a voluntary, structured questionnaire divided into three sections: demographics, symptoms/quality of life, and sources of information. Results: The dominant symptoms reported were chronic fatigue (88%), hot flashes (87%), and menstrual irregularities (85%). The areas most negatively affected by symptomatology were sleep/rest (74%) and emotional well-being (68%). The internet (46%, n=55) served as the primary source of information, surpassing healthcare professionals (n=44). Geographically, 65% of the sample resided in urban areas and 35% in rural areas, with a dominant majority being married. Discussion/Conclusions: Perimenopausal fluctuations severely impact the daily functioning of women in Albania. These findings signal an urgent need for national health education programs and the mitigation of geographical and cultural barriers. Early medical consultation remains paramount for the effective management and support of women during this transition.
